meta.description: Flags on each series' latest published month: moves of 2.5 spreads or more against the series' own ten-year history, or against its neighbours.

sources.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Economic Data
sources.licence: FRED API Terms of Use (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html). The terms require the notice "This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis", which the site prints. Series owned by third parties carry the word "Copyright" in their notes and need the owner's permission beyond personal use, so the catalogue holds only series published by US federal agencies (public domain) and the collector stops on any series whose notes say Copyright. The terms do not address storing data.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; most series are monthly
sources.typical_lag: two to eight weeks after the month ends, depending on the series

sources.name: BIS statistics (policy rates, consumer prices, exchange rates, effective exchange rates)
sources.licence: Terms of permitted use of BIS statistics (https://www.bis.org/terms_statistics.htm). Use is unrestricted provided the BIS is cited as the source, the use does not imply endorsement, and inclusion in a commercial product brings no additional charge to users. The statistics are not investment advice. The site cites the BIS under every table.

sources.name: OpenDOSM (Department of Statistics Malaysia)
sources.licence: DOSM Open Data License as shown in the OpenDOSM FAQ. It permits copying, publishing, adapting and commercial use; the datasets must not be used in a way that suggests official status or endorsement. The text was read on an archived copy of the FAQ (opendosm.netlify.app), not on open.dosm.gov.my itself, so re-read it there.

sources.name: IMF data (International Trade in Goods, International Liquidity, Consumer Price Index)
sources.licence: IMF Copyright and Usage, Special Terms for Statistical Data (https://www.imf.org/en/about/copyright-and-terms). Users may download, copy, create derivative works, publish and distribute IMF data, with attribution in the form "Source: International Monetary Fund, <dataset>, <link>", saying so when the data are materially transformed, and without altering the data in a way that affects their accuracy. Commercial reuse needs the IMF's permission (copyright@imf.org). The general site terms also forbid bulk download by automated means without permission; this pipeline asks the public SDMX API for 19 series a day, which is not a bulk download of the database, but the IMF has not been asked to confirm that. The site is non-commercial and cites the IMF under every table.
sources.typical_lag: one to five months (trade is slowest)

limitations: Figures are the latest published values and are revised by their publishers. A flag can appear or disappear when a figure is revised.
A flag means a move was large against the series' own last ten years. It does not say why the move happened or what comes next, and it is a research lead, not advice.
With a threshold of 2.5 spreads, roughly one or two readings in a hundred are flagged by chance alone, and more for series with fat tails. The backtest shows how often.

Southeast Asian series come from the BIS and the IMF, which compile them from national sources on one definition per measure. The BIS has no consumer prices, policy rate or real effective exchange rate for Vietnam (its consumer prices come from the IMF) and no policy rate for Singapore. Trade and reserves are in US dollars, so a move can be a currency move.
This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

Source: BIS statistics; FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, from US federal agencies); Department of Statistics Malaysia (OpenDOSM); International Monetary Fund, International Trade in Goods, International Liquidity and Consumer Price Index datasets (https://data.imf.org); Indeed Hiring Lab (CC BY 4.0). Surprises, flags and forecasts are this site's calculations, not the publishers'.

finding.label: observation
finding.reason: Measured moves compared with each series' own published history. No model is involved, so a flag says something unusual happened, not why, and not what comes next.

data.sentence: United States: federal funds effective rate rose 0.13 percentage points in October 2026, against a usual +0.00 percentage points for a month. That is 8.8 times its usual spread over the previous ten years.
data.label: observation

data.sentence: Vietnam: exchange rate, local currency per US dollar rose (local currency weaker) 1.13% in August 2026, against a usual +0.09% for a month. That is 5.5 times its usual spread over the previous ten years.
data.label: observation

data.sentence: Vietnam: exchange rate, local currency per US dollar moved against its neighbours in August 2026. Its surprise was +5.5 spreads while the median of 5 other Southeast Asian economies was -0.9, so it rose more than the region by a gap 3.5 times that gap's usual spread.
data.label: observation
